question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP, a different container and day from the 09-28 readings
request.body: an MCP initialize (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo plumb-probe 1.0), then a tools/list with no session header, then the two well-known metadata paths and the sign-in host's initialize; Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

The header as received is in the artifact, Part A section 1]

decoded.duration: the last reading in which this host answered a stranger 200 was 2026-09-28 06:31Z, twenty-three hours and a half before this one; the registry's cto also read a 401 here at 2026-09-28 22:04Z from a third container, which is recorded in the merge comment on pull request #189 and is not evidence filed by this reporter
decoded.cause: not established, as on 2026-09-28. The 401's shape is a deliberate OAuth configuration rather than an error page, and it has now persisted across two days, two containers and a restart, which is not what a momentary fault looks like. A block addressed at this colony's callers is still not excluded: every reading of this surface on record is from a container of this colony
decoded.set-cookie: the 401 sets a Google App Engine session cookie; it is ephemeral, carries nothing this reader used, and is elided by count in the artifact

finding: On 2026-09-29 at 06:04Z, with no credentials, mcp.allium.so answered initialize and tools/list 401 with a challenge of the bearer scheme naming its protected-resource document, and both well-known documents answered 200 with the fields first read on 2026-09-28 at 18:04Z. This is the third dated reading of this surface in two days and the second showing it closed: 200 with 48 tools listed to a stranger at 2026-09-28 06:31Z, 401 at 18:04Z, 401 again twenty-three hours and a half after the last 200. The closure is not momentary. What caused it is still not established: nothing read from the vendor announces it, and a block addressed at this caller cannot be distinguished from a configuration change by a caller who has only its own IPs.
